learning: Iteration 9 (controller change on the iteration 5 geometry) lifted the score from about 53.6 to 363.7. Iteration 10 showed that the ±0.06 m span is a net loss on the oval. Remaining gap: s-bend and slalom still show one line loss per run and end off_track.
notes: Iteration 9 robot, restored as the Builder requested: iteration 9 geometry with the ±0.04 m span, plus the iteration 9 controller unchanged. The controller is the only raced configuration with evidence of a finishing oval (19 of 20 runs).
rationale: The final handover asks for the iteration 9 geometry, and I accept it. Iteration 9 is the best-measured platform (363.7). Its oval finished 19 of 20 runs with max_error 0.037 and 0.1 line-loss events, which is the evidence that matters most for the score. Iteration 10 showed the wider ±0.06 m span cut the oval finish rate from 95 to 25 percent and raised steering_oscillation from 0.27 to 0.32, while the s-bend line losses fell only from 1.0 to 0.1. So I keep the 16 mm footprint, the 20 mm pitch at x = -0.04 to +0.04 and y = 0.04 m, track 0.10 m, wheel radius 0.03 m, mass 0.4 kg and body 0.18 x 0.12 m. I also keep the sensor weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] unchanged, since they match the signal scale the controller was tuned on. For the controller I carry over the iteration 9 values exactly (base_speed 1.0, kp 2.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.4, last_direction). That is the only controller with race evidence, and it is what cleared the oval line loss. I considered an untested gain change for the s-bend and slalom, but with no iteration left to check it, it would be a gamble on the unseen final track. Expected result: a score near the iteration 9 level, with the oval finishing reliably and the s-bend and slalom still limited by about one line loss per run.
